doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Gil Evans teaching the band bebop phrasing
summary: Konitz describes Gil Evans as the band's philosopher and how he taught phrasing, with remarks on the 'Donna Lee' arrangement.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Did you and Gil hang out much when you were on the band? Was he traveling with the band?

Sometimes, yeah. He was kind of the band philosopher, he and Billy [Eckstine], so we enjoyed hanging out and sharing philosophies and things like that. He was pretty much the leader of the band, especially when he was teaching the band how to play phrases, the bebop music.
How did he teach the band to play those things?

Just by talking about the accent part of the articulation and the legato part of it as I recall, and pretty much just reviewing it enough times to get them to get some feeling for it. I don’t remember any very intricate teaching methods, except that I mentioned.
I’m always stunned when I hear that chart on Donna Lee because he’s got three trumpets and cup mutes and five clarinets all playing that head in unison.
Just to get five clarinets to play in tune, playing anything, is pretty stunning.
